evidence.method: read each package.json; license falls back to the first SPDX identifier found in a LICENSE/COPYING file; entry = dsh.bundle.patch + dsh.client + main + an index file
limits: a license declared in package.json is taken at face value; the text itself was not diffed against the declared SPDX id
classification below is rule-based and marks a package unknown when a rule cannot decide
third-party plugins are not in either root: the external set lives in the desktop install profile and in the vendored recon trees, which this run did not scan

rules.as_is: no @deepseek-ai dependency name outside a set the 0.2.1 surface declares, and no cordis patch of its own
rules.translate: declares at least one @deepseek-ai/* dependency; a rename is the plausible fix
rules.shim: is a client-half package (dsh.client) whose contract is the client module table
rules.rewrite: ships its own cordis patch row (dsh.bundle.patch), so its contract is a composition row
rules.unknown: none of the above could be decided from the manifest alone

findings.fact: the packaged tree at Q: contains @deepseek-ai packages versioned 0.1.5-rc.1 (e.g. @deepseek-ai/dsh-base@0.1.5-rc.1), so it is the 0.1.5 official install, not a 0.2.x one
both surveyed roots contain only @deepseek-ai/* packages: they are kernel/official packages, so this survey describes the official surface, not third-party plugins
